title: Successive transposes through the canonical finite derived compositor
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. For a $k$-scheme $T$, put $D(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the ordinary unbounded derived category on its small pro-etale site. For a scheme map $u$ use $P_u=Lu^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ and the canonical adjunction $P_u\dashv R_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}B$ be morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the canonical constant-ring identifications, whose composition is [lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition], and the canonical pullback comparison $\alpha_{f,g}:P_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fP_g$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Let $\kappa_{g,f}:R_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_gR_f$ be exactly the finite-level K-injective compositor of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]; the normalization of the ringed comparison is that of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], rather than an arbitrary adjunction on isomorphic functors. For $M\in D(B)$, $Q\in D(Y)$, $N\in D(X)$ and arbitrary arrows $w:M\to R_gQ$, $v:Q\to R_fN$, put
$$h=\kappa_{g,f,N}^{-1}\circ R_g(v)\circ w:M\to R_{gf}N,$$
$$\widehat w=\varepsilon_{g,Q}\circ P_g(w),\qquad \widehat v=\varepsilon_{f,N}\circ P_f(v).$$
Let $\widehat{\ }^{\mathrm{comp}}$ denote transposition by the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Then, as morphisms $P_{gf}M\to N$,
$$\varepsilon_{gf,N}\circ P_{gf}(h)=\widehat{\kappa_{g,f,N}\circ h}^{\mathrm{comp}}\circ\alpha_{f,g,M}
=\widehat v\circ P_f(\widehat w)\circ\alpha_{f,g,M}.$$
In particular the successive transpose of $R_g(v)\circ w$ is $\widehat v\circ P_f(\widehat w)$ with the specified canonical comparisons. There are no properness, boundedness or constructibility assumptions on the maps or objects.

proof.text: The finite coefficient inverse image is exact, and its right adjoint preserves K-injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. The ordinary upperStarComp is defined by conjugating lowerStarComp under the adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so its conjugacy premise is immediate by the conjugation equivalence [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Apply the proved source specialization of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], Adjunction.rightDerivedFunctorCompIso'_hom_eq_conjugateEquiv, to these three adjunctions. This identifies the inverse of the specified finiteDirectImageComposition of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] with the conjugate of the exact-map derived pullback compositor.

proof.text: Compare each exact-map derived adjunction with the K-flat derived adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The lemma Adjunction.derived_eq_ofNatIsoLeft compares them using the factorization leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_fac of the left-derived counit. Both adjunctions are induced by the same ordinary adjunction through [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived]. Substitute these three adjunction equalities in the previous conjugacy equation. Expanding conjugation and the canonical leftDerivedFunctorNatIso and leftDerivedFunctorCompIso identifies its left comparison with exactly leftDerivedUpperStarComp of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. This proves the private helper derived_compositor_conjugate without constructing any ringed-topos comparison system.

proof.text: For any two adjunctions a and b and left natural transformation c, conjugateEquiv_counit of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] followed by naturality of c proves L'(h;conjugate(c));epsilon_b = c_M;transpose_a(h). Apply this to the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the composite-morphism adjunction, with h=w;R_g(v). Substitute the inverse-compositor conjugacy equation from the previous steps. The right-hand input in the first displayed equality simplifies to h by cancellation of kappa inverse with kappa, giving that equality.

proof.text: Use Adjunction.comp_homEquiv from [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to expand the inverse composite Hom bijection into the successive inverse Hom bijections. Naturality of the inverse Hom bijection in the right-hand object moves v outside the first transpose. The counit formula Adjunction.homEquiv_counit then gives exactly P_f(P_g(w);epsilon_g);P_f(v);epsilon_f. This is the final asserted clause. Precompose it with the pullback comparison and cancel kappa inverse with kappa inside the Hom bijection to obtain the second displayed equality. The calculation applies to all objects of the ordinary unbounded derived categories.
